title: Analyzing the Optimization Conflict Between Image- and Text-Based Person Re-Identification
abstract: arXiv:2606.02242v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Unifying image-based (I2I) and text-based (T2I) person re-identification (ReID) within a single model is complicated by a fundamental conflict between their training objectives. While I2I ReID focuses on identity-level invariance across images of the same person captured by multiple cameras, T2I ReID is driven by instance-specific textual descriptions tied to unique visual traits. When both objectives are optimized on a shared vision encoder, they impose opposing requirements on the same embeddings - I2I contracts intra-identity distances while T2I requires them to persist - so improving one task's representation actively degrades the other's. This paper analyzes this optimization conflict and shows empirically that the two objectives are not jointly satisfiable by a single unconstrained encoder. translated_title: 分析基于图像与基于文本的行人重识别之间的优化冲突
translated_abstract: 在单一模型中统一基于图像的（I2I）与基于文本的（T2I）行人重识别（ReID）任务，会受到二者训练目标之间根本性冲突的阻碍。I2I ReID 关注的是由多个摄像头拍摄的同一个人的图像间的身份级不变性，而 T2I ReID 则由与独特视觉特征绑定的实例级文本描述驱动。当这两个目标在同一个共享视觉编码器上被同时优化时，它们会对相同的嵌入施加相互对立的要求——I2I 需要收缩同身份内部的距离，而 T2I 则要求这些距离保持不变——因此提升一个任务的表征会主动损害另一个任务的性能。本文对这一优化冲突进行了分析，并通过实验证明，这两个目标无法由单个无约束的编码器同时满足。基于这一发现，我们通过一个受控的两阶段流水线来研究该冲突：共享视觉编码器首先被训练……
tldr: 本文实证揭示了基于图像与基于文本的行人重识别在共享视觉编码器上存在根本性的优化冲突——两种任务对嵌入空间提出相互对立的要求，无法由单一无约束编码器同时满足。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically demonstrates a fundamental optimization conflict between image-based and text-based person ReID, showing that their opposing training objectives on a shared vision encoder cannot be jointly satisfied by a single unconstrained encoder.
